target: Cabe señalar que esta medida beneficiará a miles de personas.
english: It should be pointed out that this measure will benefit thousands of people.
tip: 'Cabe señalar' – literally 'it fits to point out'. Caber (to fit) builds formal Spanish's favorite hedge: cabe destacar, cabe mencionar = it's worth noting.

target: Le hace falta descansar.
english: He needs to rest.
tip: 'Hace falta' is literally 'it makes a lack'. The needer is an indirect object: 'Le hace falta descansar' = rest is lacking to him. Needs happen TO you in Spanish.

target: Llevo dos horas esperando el autobús.
english: I've been waiting for the bus for two hours.
tip: Two hours and still waiting? Spanish uses plain present for ongoing time: 'Llevo dos horas esperando' – literally 'I carry two hours waiting'. No 'have been' needed.

target: Quienquiera que haya dicho eso, se equivoca.
english: Whoever said that is wrong.
tip: Quienquiera que + subjunctive = whoever.

target: Quisiera una mesa junto a la ventana.
english: I'd like a table by the window.
tip: 'Quisiera una mesa' softens the ask with past subjunctive – like 'I should like'. Plain 'quiero' isn't rude, just blunt – quisiera adds the 'could I...?' courtesy.

target: Si tuviera vacaciones, visitaría a mi abuela.
english: If I had vacation, I would visit my grandmother.
tip: English brains want 'si tendría' – banned. After si it's past subjunctive: 'Si tuviera vacaciones'. The conditional (visitaría) lives only in the result half.

target: Ellos se hablan por teléfono cada noche.
english: They talk to each other on the phone every night.
tip: Se hablan could in theory mean 'they each talk to themselves' – Spanish uses one se for reflexive AND reciprocal. The nightly phone call makes it mutual; el uno al otro would force 'each other.'

target: Les pedí que me despertaran a las seis.
english: I asked them to wake me up at six.
tip: You can't 'ask someone to do' in Spanish – no infinitive allowed. Pedir forces a que-clause: 'pedí que me despertaran', literally 'I asked that they wake me'.

target: Estará cansado después de un viaje tan largo.
english: He must be tired after such a long trip.
tip: 'Estará cansado' isn't a prediction – it's a guess. Spanish future tense doubles as 'must be / probably is': he's tired, I bet. Context, not 'will', decides.

target: Ojalá hubiera aprovechado más el tiempo cuando era joven.
english: I wish I had made better use of my time when I was young.
tip: Ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive for impossible past wishes.

target: Aunque me ofrecieran el doble, no volvería.
english: Even if they offered me double, I wouldn't go back.
tip: Aunque + imperfect subjunctive for hypothetical concession.

target: Aquí se habla español.
english: Spanish is spoken here.
tip: "Se" impersonal: no specific subject. "Se vive bien aquí" = One lives well here / People live well here. Like English "one" or "people."

target: Estas camisetas se venden muy bien.
english: These shirts sell very well.
tip: Passive se: the verb agrees with the grammatical subject. "Se venden camisetas" (camisetas = subject, plural → venden).

target: Me tocó el asiento del medio.
english: I got stuck with the middle seat.
tip: Stuck with the middle seat? "Me tocó" – tocar means it fell to you by luck of the draw. Lottery wins, chores, and "el asiento del medio" all just "te tocan."

target: Se vive bien en esta ciudad.
english: You live well in this city.
tip: "Se vive" = one lives / people live. Impersonal se with intransitive verbs: "Se vive bien aquí" = People live well here.

target: La decisión fue tomada sin consultar al equipo.
english: The decision was made without consulting the team.
tip: Passive with ser + past participle (tomada agrees with decisión).

target: El taxista mencionó que conocía un atajo para evitar el tráfico.
english: The taxi driver mentioned he knew a shortcut to avoid traffic.
tip: Reported speech: "conozco" → "conocía" (present → imperfect) after "mencionó que."

target: Nos ofrecieron un vuelo alternativo porque el nuestro fue cancelado por condiciones meteorológicas adversas.
english: They offered us an alternative flight because ours was canceled due to adverse weather conditions.
tip: 'Nuestro/nuestra' agrees with the thing possessed, not the possessor: 'nuestra oficina' (fem.) vs. 'nuestro equipo' (masc.).

target: ¿Qué harías si ganaras la lotería?
english: What would you do if you won the lottery?
tip: Tempted by "si ganarías"? Never – si refuses the would-form. The hypothesis takes past subjunctive, "si ganaras la lotería," and "harías" stays outside the if.

target: Si hubiera aceptado ese trabajo, viviría en Madrid.
english: If I had accepted that job, I'd be living in Madrid.
tip: Past choice, present result – mix the halves: "si hubiera aceptado" (back then) pairs with "viviría en Madrid" (right now). No rule forces hubiera to match habría.

target: Si bien la casa es pequeña, es suficiente para nosotros.
english: Although the house is small, it's enough for us.
tip: "Si bien" isn't "if well" – it's a formal although, and no subjunctive follows: "si bien la casa es pequeña" keeps plain "es." It states a fact, not a condition.

target: Mi dormitorio es tranquilo porque da a un patio interior.
english: My bedroom is peaceful because it overlooks an inner courtyard.
tip: "Da a un patio": the room literally "gives onto" a courtyard. Spanish uses dar a for whatever a window or room faces – no special verb like "overlooks" needed.

target: Cabe destacar que la hospitalidad fue lo mejor del viaje.
english: It's worth noting that the hospitality was the best part of the trip.
tip: Cabe comes from caber, to fit: literally 'it fits to highlight that...' – there's room for this remark. That fit-logic powers the whole formal family: cabe mencionar, cabe señalar.

target: Acaba de llamar tu madre.
english: Your mother just called.
tip: English needs a past tense ('just called'), but Spanish stays in the present: acaba de llamar – roughly 'she finishes-from calling.' The just-happened feel lives in acabar de, not the tense.

target: Llevo viajando por España tres semanas.
english: I've been traveling around Spain for three weeks.
tip: Llevo is literally 'I carry': llevo viajando tres semanas = 'I carry three weeks traveling.' Spanish uses llevar + gerund for ongoing duration – no perfect tense needed.

target: Se aceptan tarjetas de crédito y débito.
english: Credit and debit cards are accepted.
tip: Why plural 'aceptan'? In passive se the cards are the subject – they 'accept themselves'. The verb agrees with tarjetas, not with an invisible 'we'.

target: Acabo de hablar con mi madre y esta muy contenta.
english: I just spoke to my mother and she's very happy.
tip: Acabar normally means 'to finish,' but acabo de hablar isn't 'I finish talking' – the de flips it to 'I just spoke.' Acabar alone ends actions; acabar de + infinitive timestamps them.

target: Se pusieron a discutir en medio del restaurante.
english: They started arguing in the middle of the restaurant.
tip: 'Discutir' is a false friend: it usually means to argue, not discuss. Se pusieron a discutir = a heated quarrel, not a debate. Calm discussing is hablar de.

target: Se nota a la legua que está enamorado.
english: You can tell from a mile off that he's in love.
tip: 'A la legua' = from a league away, an old road unit about an hour's walk. Spanish measures obviousness as distance: his love shows from miles off.

target: Siempre que tenga la oportunidad, viajo a nuevos lugares.
english: Whenever I have the opportunity, I travel to new places.
tip: One trigger, two meanings: 'siempre que tenga' (subjunctive) = if/whenever I ever get the chance – not yet real. With indicative it would just report a habit.
